sections.h2: What makes selling a house in Rochester Hills, Michigan different?
sections.html:
Rochester Hills is a high-value suburb in Oakland County, so the paperwork is usually smaller than the price tag: a deed recorded with the county, two affidavits filed at the city's Assessing Department, and a tax certificate from the county treasurer. The city's own home-sale rules are light, and most of the work happens at the county and state level.

The city sits about 25 miles north of downtown Detroit. The first European settler arrived in 1817, Avon Township was organized in 1835, and voters approved a city charter in 1984, when the township became the City of Rochester Hills. The older city of Rochester is a separate municipality that sits beside it and incorporated in 1967, which matters because many buyers use the two names loosely.

This page covers who handles what, what the county charges, and how the city's tax calendar affects a closing.

sections.h2: How big is Rochester Hills and what do the Census numbers say?
sections.html:
Rochester Hills has 32.80 square miles of land, a density of about 2,326 people per square mile, and a July 2025 Census Bureau estimate of 77,539 residents, up 1.6 percent from the 2020 base of 76,321.

Two lines stand out. More than three of every four homes are owner-occupied, so there is little rental stock to compete with a seller's listing. And 23.6 percent of residents speak a language other than English at home, which is worth remembering when you plan showings and write the listing.

sections.h2: Where do Rochester Hills buyers send their children to school?
sections.html:
Rochester Community Schools serve most of the city, with Rochester Adams High School, Rochester High School and Stoney Creek High School all inside the city limits. Part of Rochester Hills falls in the Avondale School District instead, where many addresses are zoned to Deer Field Elementary in the city, while others go to Auburn Elementary in Auburn Hills or Woodland Elementary in Troy.

All Avondale residents attend Avondale Middle School in Rochester Hills and Avondale High School in Auburn Hills. Because an address on the same street can belong to a different district, ask the district for an official boundary check before you promise a school in a listing.

Higher education adds another buyer group. Oakland University and Rochester Christian University both offer programs in the city, and the Rochester Hills Public Library, which the city runs, is open to residents of the city of Rochester and Oakland Township by contract.

sections.h2: What should I know about the land and the borders?
sections.html:
Rochester Hills is rolling, as the name suggests. Elevation climbs from about 690 feet in the southeast to 1,032 feet in the northwest, and the Clinton River and Paint Creek were the water sources that drew the first settlers.

The city's neighbors are:

  • Oakland Charter Township to the north, along Dutton Road.
  • Troy to the south, along South Boulevard.
  • Shelby Township in Macomb County to the east, along Dequindre Road, with the city of Rochester partly on the eastern edge.
  • Auburn Hills to the west, along part of Adams Road.

Rochester Hills has no police department of its own. The Oakland County Sheriff's Office provides police service, and the 52nd District Court's third division sits in the city. If a buyer asks about local services, point them to the city's website and the sheriff's office rather than guessing at response times.

sections.h2: What do I file with the Rochester Hills Assessing Department after a sale?
sections.html:
The buyer files a Property Transfer Affidavit and a Principal Residence Exemption affidavit with the Assessing Department at 1000 Rochester Hills Drive, in person or by mail. The city says the closing agent should hand the buyer both forms, and the office is open Monday through Friday from 8:00 am to 5:00 pm.

The Principal Residence Exemption removes up to 18 mills of school tax from a bill if the owner lives in the home as a main residence. The seller should ask the Assessing Department for the form that rescinds the exemption on the home being sold, so it ends at the right date. Assessing also lists disabled veteran and poverty exemptions, and the poverty exemption must be filed again each year.

If a buyer wants a quick tax estimate, the city gives a method: take half of the estimated property value and multiply it by the current millage rate. Assessing can run that estimate for a prospective buyer. Owners who think a value is too high have one chance a year, at the March Board of Review, after the notice arrives in February.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Oakland County?
sections.html:
The Oakland County Register of Deeds charges $30.00 per deed, and that figure already includes the $4.00 state survey and remonumentation fee. Add $3.00 for each extra recorded reference on a discharge or assignment, and $1.00 per page for copies.

Warranty deeds, land contracts and any deed with a covenant of warranty must be tax certified at the Oakland County Treasurer's Office for $5.00. If you mail documents, the Register of Deeds can obtain the certificate for you when the $5.00 is included in the payment. The county says hand-carried documents take about two weeks to come back, mailed ones two to four weeks.

Transfer tax is figured on the full price. The county prints its rates as $0.55 per $500 for the county ($1.10 per $1,000) and $3.75 per $500 for the state ($7.50 per $1,000). Documents with consideration under $100 are exempt, and any other exemption has to be shown on the face of the deed. Under MCL 207.523 the seller owes the tax.

sections.h2: How do Rochester Hills tax due dates affect my closing?
sections.html:
Rochester Hills bills twice a year, and the summer bill carries school and county taxes only. The city's page shows summer taxes payable from July 1 to September 14 with 1 percent interest added on September 15, and winter taxes payable from December 1 through a mid-February due date.

  • For the 2026 tax year the city lists a winter due date of February 16, 2027, with a 3 percent penalty added soon after.
  • Unpaid taxes turn delinquent on March 2 and move to the Oakland County Treasurer.
  • Postmarks are not honored, so a late-closing payment should be made in person or online.
  • Online payment by e-check carries no fee; cards, Apple Pay and Google Pay carry a 2.75 percent processing fee.

The winter bill includes the city's own levy for police and fire services, local roads and the library, and a closing in the fall or winter may happen before it is paid. Ask the title company who will pay it and how it is credited. Treasury's property tax look-up shows the status of each bill by parcel.

faqs.q: Which office records a deed for a Rochester Hills house?
faqs.a: The Oakland County Register of Deeds. It charges $30.00 per document, including the $4.00 state survey fee, and it needs a $5.00 treasurer tax certificate on warranty deeds.

faqs.q: Does the city of Rochester Hills require an inspection before I sell?
faqs.a: Ask the city's Building Department whether any inspection applies to your address before you set a closing date. The Assessing Department deals with tax forms.

faqs.q: What does the buyer file with the city after closing?
faqs.a: A Property Transfer Affidavit, plus a Principal Residence Exemption affidavit if the buyer will live there. Both go to the Assessing Department at 1000 Rochester Hills Drive.

faqs.q: When are Rochester Hills property taxes due?
faqs.a: Summer taxes are due September 14. Winter taxes are due in mid-February, shown as February 16, 2027 for the 2026 bill, and unpaid bills go to Oakland County on March 2.

faqs.q: Is the transfer tax paid by the seller in Rochester Hills?
faqs.a: Yes. Michigan law puts the transfer tax on the seller, at $3.75 per $500 for the state and $0.55 per $500 for the county.
